module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 674

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/674](https://www.erdosproblems.com/674)
- [Ko40] Ko, Chao, *Note on the Diophantine equation $x^xy^y=z^z$*. J. Chinese Math. Soc.
  (1940), 31-39.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos674

/-- The set of integer solutions to $x^x y^y = z^z$ with $x, y, z > 1$. -/
def solutionSet : Set (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) :=
  {(x, y, z) | 1 < x ∧ 1 < y ∧ 1 < z ∧ x ^ x * y ^ y = z ^ z}

/--
Are there any integer solutions to $x^xy^y=z^z$ with $x,y,z>1$?

Ko [Ko40] proved there are none if $(x,y)=1$, but there are in fact infinitely many solutions in
general - for example, $x=2^{12}3^6$, $y = 2^83^8$, and $z = 2^{11}3^7$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos674.lean"]
theorem erdos_674 : answer(True) ↔ solutionSet.Nonempty := by
  sorry

/--
There are in fact infinitely many integer solutions to $x^xy^y=z^z$ with $x,y,z>1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos674.lean"]
theorem erdos_674.variants.infinite : solutionSet.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos674

findings.description: The module docstring's reference entry reads "[Ko40] Ko, Chao, *Note on the Diophantine equation $x^xy^y=z^z$*. J. Chinese Math. Soc. (1940), 31-39." The pages are wrong and the volume is missing. The paper is J. Chinese Math. Soc. vol. 2 (1940), pp. 205–207. Neither MathSciNet nor zbMATH lists any 1940 paper by Ko with pages 31–39. The mathematics is unaffected. The entry follows erdosproblems.com's bibliography format, so the slip may come from the site's bib entry, which I could not retrieve (Cloudflare blocks it and the Wayback Machine has no copy).
findings.source_evidence: MathSciNet MR0004251 (MR Lookup, reviewed by P. Erdős): AUTHOR = {Ko, Chao}, TITLE = {Note on the Diophantine equation x^xy^y=z^z}, JOURNAL = {J. Chinese Math. Soc.}, VOLUME = {2}, YEAR = {1940}, PAGES = {205--207}. zbMATH Zbl 0061.07010 (https://zbmath.org/3099696): "J. Chin. Math. Soc. 2, 205-207 (1940)." MR and zbMATH author searches for Ko, Chao, 1936–1941, show no paper with pp. 31–39.
findings.suggested_fix: - [Ko40] Ko, Chao, *Note on the Diophantine equation $x^xy^y=z^z$*. J. Chinese Math. Soc. 2 (1940), 205–207.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for integer solutions with x,y,z > 1. The Lean set contains triples in ℕ × ℕ × ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Integers greater than 1 are exactly the naturals greater than 1, and the equation is the same on both. The integer solution set {(x,y,z) : ℤ³ | 1<x ∧ 1<y ∧ 1<z ∧ x^x.toNat*y^y.toNat = z^z.toNat} is the image of solutionSet under the injective coordinate-wise cast ℕ³ → ℤ³. So the ℤ version is nonempty (resp. infinite) exactly when solutionSet is. This covers both erdos_674 and erdos_674.variants.infinite. Proved in scratch as image_eq, nonempty_iff and infinite_iff, using standard axioms only.

https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html (Erdős paper list; 1979-21.pdf and 1979-22.pdf downloaded, but they are image scans with no text layer)

review.notes:
No mathematical defect found. The only finding is the citation slip above.

What I checked in Lean (scratch files in /workspace/review):
(1) Ko's example (2^12·3^6, 2^8·3^8, 2^11·3^7) is in solutionSet (`decide +kernel`). From this, `True ↔ solutionSet.Nonempty` follows, which is exactly `erdos_674` with answer(True). This matches the source: "solved in the affirmative".
(2) The linked plby proof, compiled against the repository's own `Erdos674.solutionSet` on this toolchain (Lean v4.33.1), proves `solutionSet.Infinite` with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The only side effect is a deprecation warning for `Set.mem_setOf_eq`. Its family is the one the source gives (a=2^{n+1}, b=2^n−1).
(3) The trivial solution (1,2,2) is excluded. A brute-force search finds no solutions with 2 ≤ x,y,z ≤ 80.

The categories (both `research solved`) and the lean4 formal_proof records agree with the source's "PROVED (LEAN)" status. The forum shows Bhavik Mehta's Lean solution of 9 Dec 2025, and the linked file credits him.

Non-mathematical points a maintainer might want to look at:
- The formal_proof URL points at `blob/main`, not at a commit permalink. PROOFS.md asks for a stable link.
- The module docstring does not cite [Er79], the original Erdős source named by erdosproblems.com.
- The source adds an open follow-up that the file does not formalize: "In [Er79] Erdős asked if the infinite families found by Ko are the only solutions." Mills settled the cases 4xy ≥ z^2, and 4xy < z^2 is still open. It could be added as an open variant. Leaving a variant out is not a misformalization.

I could not read Er79 itself: the Rényi archive scans have no text layer and no OCR is available. Faithfulness was settled against the cited source, erdosproblems.com/674, whose wording has not changed since at least September 2025.
